title: Methodology invariant x agent capability matrix
modeNote: Data consumed by `arggon doctor`. No rule logic lives here: the rows DECLARE which native mechanism each agent uses for each methodology invariant, and `gap: true` means the agent's adapter surface delivers that invariant natively or not at all. The kernel (@arggondev/lib) behind the arggon CLI stays the enforcement of record on every row, and a gap row is advisory in every surface - never blocking in CI or in a transition.

fieldNotes.invariants[].statement: Verbatim clause from the carriers' `- **Invariants:**` header block (agents.md / engineering.md / convention.md).
fieldNotes.rows[].mechanism: The native client feature used, agent-namespaced (`opencode:` / `zcode:` / `claude:`), or `docs + CLI floor:` where the shipped docs plus the arggon CLI/kernel are the whole mechanism.
fieldNotes.rows[].package: The client package whose native surface carries the mechanism (`opencode`, `zcode`); `none` where no client mechanism exists and the docs + CLI floor carries the invariant.
fieldNotes.rows[].gap: true when the agent has no shipped adapter surface delivering the invariant - the note says what is missing and what enforces it meanwhile.
fieldNotes.rows[].note: Required non-empty for every gap row (schema-gated); null otherwise.

invariants.statement: humans and agents follow the same rules

agents.adapter: generated plugin bundle `templates/docs/zcode/arggon/` (`arggon mcp`, commands, agents, hooks) installed through the local marketplace
docs pointer only: `CLAUDE.md` -> `@AGENTS.md` (no plugin bundle yet; spec S6 follow-on story)

rows.mechanism: opencode:tool.transform registers the native `arggon` tools (Code Mode `tools.arggon.*`), each calling the same kernel operation the CLI's --json path runs and returning the documented envelope

opencode:worktree domain (`ctx.worktree.create/list/refresh/remove`) through tools.arggon.start/branch/cleanup; every tracker mutation auto-commits only the files it wrote, and the generated pre-commit gate runs `arggon validate`

opencode:permissions - generated deny rules in opencode.jsonc (force-push, `commit --no-verify`) plus the per-agent tool allow-lists in .opencode/agents/*.md (reviewer cannot edit, worker cannot nest); kernel refusals arrive as typed tool errors

opencode:session.hook("context") re-injects the bounded (1 KiB) active work-item block built from `arggon show --meta --json`, and the generated .opencode/commands/arggon-* carry the same playbook as the docs

opencode:tool.transform — the kernel operation refuses a stolen claim and every reopen on all paths (native tools, CLI, MCP); the generated worker/reviewer agent contracts state the rule and tools.arggon.cleanup releases a dropped claim
zcode:mcp - the plugin bundle registers `arggon mcp`, whose tools return the identical envelopes from the same kernel operations as the CLI (schema parity test-gated)
zcode:mcp - arggon_start (claim + worktree), arggon_branch and arggon_cleanup drive the same kernel commit/worktree path; the plugin never writes a tracker file itself

zcode:plugin.hooks.PreToolUse (hooks/gate.mjs) denies force-push and `commit --no-verify` for every session and holds the reviewer backstop window; fail-open by design, so the kernel stays the enforcement of record
zcode:plugin bundle — the generated commands/, agents/ (coordinator, worker, reviewer) and the `arggon-cli` skill, refreshed by `arggon init` with provenance and never overwriting adopter edits
zcode:mcp - the kernel refuses a stolen claim and every reopen, and the reviewer backstop denies the mutating mcp__arggon__* tools (arggon_comment stays open as the verdict channel)
docs + CLI floor: CLAUDE.md points at @AGENTS.md, and the agent runs the arggon CLI, whose kernel holds the rules; there is no plugin and no native tool surface
rows.note: no adapters/claude/ plugin bundle (skills, agents, hooks, commands, `arggon mcp` wiring): the parity bar is filed as the spec S6 follow-on story, so on this client the methodology is docs plus the CLI.

rows.mechanism: docs + CLI floor: git runs on the Claude Code shell and tracker mutations go through the arggon CLI, which commits exactly the files it wrote
rows.note: no client-side seam: a plugin bundle would register the arggon tools so item mutations never depend on the agent hand-writing shell commands correctly.

rows.mechanism: docs + CLI floor: the generated pre-commit hook and CI run `arggon validate`; nothing is enforced inside the client
rows.note: no claude:plugin.hooks.PreToolUse gate and no permission wiring - the OpenCode deny rules and the ZCode PreToolUse gate have no Claude Code equivalent today, so the kernel, pre-commit and CI carry it alone.

rows.mechanism: docs + CLI floor: the agent reads CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and pulls item context itself with `arggon show`
rows.note: no session hook injects the active work item (the OpenCode `session.hook('context')` block), so the agent has to ask for the context instead of receiving it.

rows.mechanism: docs + CLI floor: the kernel refuses a stolen claim and every reopen on the CLI path, and the playbook the agent reads states the rule
rows.note: no client-side backstop (no ZCode reviewer window, no OpenCode per-agent permissions): enforcement rests on the kernel alone on this client.
